block_label: Bring group in and set tone
what_to_say: “Today is about seeing before moving. Do not guess. Do not rush. We are going to stay calm, stay balanced, and make good decisions.”
what_to_explain:
Tell athletes:
today is not about speed first
today is about control first
if they rush, they are wrong
if they stay calm and see clearly, they are right
what_to_watch:
are athletes listening
are they talking over you
are they already distracted
what_to_fix: If attention is poor:“Eyes here. Listen first.”

what_to_explain: “You need enough room to move in stance without hitting anyone.”
what_to_watch:
spacing
athletes too close
athletes standing flat footed
what_to_fix: If spacing is poor:“Take two steps back.”“Spread out more.”

what_to_say: “Everybody in stance. Start moving. Small steps only. Forward, backward, left, right.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
feet should not cross
knees slightly bent
hands up
chin down
movement should be quiet and controlled
what_to_watch:
crossing feet
standing too tall
hands dropping
heavy stomping
athletes bouncing wildly
what_to_fix:
If feet cross:“Smaller steps.”
If standing too tall:“Bend your knees a little.”
If hands drop:“Hands up while you move.”
If movement is too wild:“Calm feet. Stay under control.”

what_to_say:
“When I say jab, throw one clean jab and keep moving. Do not stop after the punch.”
Call:
“Jab”
“Move”
“Jab”
“Move”
“Double jab”
“Move”
“Body jab”
“Move”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
jab should be straight
do not fall forward
after punching, recover stance immediately
movement continues after punch
what_to_watch:
leaning on jab
feet freezing after jab
dropping rear hand
overreaching
what_to_fix:
If they lean:“Touch with it, do not fall into it.”
If they freeze after jab:“Punch then reset your feet.”
If rear hand drops:“Other hand stays home.”
If overreaching:“Punch from balance.”

what_to_say:
“Now when I say slip left or slip right, move your head only a small amount. Do not jump out of position.”
Call:
“Slip left”
“Move”
“Slip right”
“Jab”
“Slip left”
“Body jab”
Add fake pauses and fake cues.
Then ask one athlete:“What did you see before you moved?”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
a slip is small, not dramatic
eyes stay up
head moves first
you are not guessing off sound alone
what_to_watch:
slipping too far
bending at waist too much
stepping when they should slip
reacting before cue is clear
panic movement
what_to_fix:
If slip is too big:“Smaller. Just off line.”
If bending too much:“Eyes up. Small move.”
If feet move first:“Head first.”
If they react blindly:“See it first. Do not guess.”

what_to_say: “One person jabs slow. One person slips. This is a control drill, not a speed drill.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
jab is light
slip is small
pause is real
return jab is straight
reset every rep
what_to_watch:
pair spacing
athletes who are too close
athletes who are already too fast
what_to_fix:
If too close:“One step back.”
If already rushing:“Slow down before we even start.”

what_to_say: “Watch the pause. That is the important part. Slip, pause, answer.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
the pause teaches control
we are not trying to beat the punch with speed
we are learning to stay calm and correct
what_to_watch:
are athletes watching
are they nodding but not understanding
what_to_fix: Ask:“Who goes first? What does the defender do?”Make them answer before starting.

what_to_say:
“Round 1. Slip and pause only. No jab back yet. Ready. Go.”
What athletes do
Partner A throws one slow jab
Partner B slips outside
Partner B pauses
reset
repeat
what_to_watch:
head movement size
balance
feet moving first
jab speed from feeder
reset discipline
what_to_fix:
If feeder too fast:“Feeder slow down. Help your partner learn.”
If slip too large:“Make it smaller.”
If defender moves feet first:“Head first.”
If no pause:“Freeze longer. Show me the pause.”
What to explain during round
Walk and say:“This pause is control.”“Do not rush the answer.”“Stay under yourself.”

what_to_say: “Stop. Good. Now add the jab return. Same slow pace.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
slip first
pause second
jab third
reset last
what_to_watch:
who is understanding sequence
who needs another demonstration
what_to_fix: If confused:Demonstrate again immediately.

what_to_say: “Go. Slip, pause, jab back, reset.”
what_to_watch:
pause disappearing
jab becoming wide
leaning on counter
poor reset
what_to_fix:
If they fire back instantly:“Pause first.”
If jab loops:“Straight back.”
If leaning:“Stay balanced.”
If no reset:“Back to start every rep.”
What to explain while coaching
“You are not trying to win. You are trying to answer correctly.”“Small movement, clean return.”

what_to_say: “Now if you are doing well, add a small angle step after the jab. If not, keep the basic version.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
only advanced athletes add angle
angle is small
do not sacrifice balance for extra movement
what_to_watch:
who is ready to progress
who should stay basic
what_to_fix: If someone adds angle badly:“Take angle out. Go back to basic.”

what_to_say: “Go. Slip, pause, jab, small angle, reset.”
what_to_watch:
quality of angle
balance after angle
overcomplication
what_to_fix:
If angle becomes jumpy:“Smaller step.”“Do not hop.”
If form falls apart:“Remove the angle.”

what_to_say: “Good. That was control first. Now we add decision making. You must say what you see before you move.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
eyes must lead action
calling the punch forces awareness
reacting without seeing is guessing
what_to_watch:
attention during transition
athletes chatting and losing focus
what_to_fix: “Eyes here. Next drill.”

what_to_say: “One partner throws jab or jab cross. The other partner must say what they see out loud before reacting. If you do not say it, it does not count.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
call must be loud enough for coach to hear
call happens before reaction
response must stay controlled
what_to_watch:
confusion about options
quiet athletes
what_to_fix: Ask:“What do you say if you see the jab?”“What do you say if you see the cross?”

what_to_say: “Say it. Then solve it.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
exact counter is less important than clear seeing and controlled answer
first priority is recognition
what_to_watch:
athlete understanding
attention level
what_to_fix: If confused:Keep only jab for first round.

what_to_say: “Go. Feeder throws jab only first. Responder says ‘jab’ before reacting.”
what_to_watch:
can you hear calls
timing of calls
freezing
guessing
feeder speed
what_to_fix:
If call too quiet:“Louder.”
If reacting before speaking:“Say it first.”
If freezing:“Feeder slower.”
If feeder fast:“Help your partner learn.”
What to explain during round
“Your eyes should lead your hands.”“Correct first, fast later.”

what_to_say: “Now feeder can choose jab or jab cross. Responder must call what they see.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
cross call matters when second punch appears
stay calm if sequence changes
do not rush because you are unsure
what_to_watch: who got overwhelmed in Round 1
what_to_fix: Keep simpler version for struggling pairs.

what_to_say: “Go. Say it, then solve it.”
what_to_watch:
silent reactions
wrong calls
wrong responses
panic
balance
what_to_fix:
If silent:“Does not count. Say it.”
If wrong call:“What did you actually see?”
If panic:“Slow down and see clearly.”
If balance breaks:“Stay under control.”
What to explain while coaching
“It is okay to be slower if you are accurate.”“Do not guess to be fast.”

what_to_say: “If your pair is doing well, feeder can change timing a little. If not, keep it steady.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
random timing increases thinking load
but only if control is still present
what_to_watch: whether randomness improves drill or ruins it
what_to_fix: If too messy:“Back to steady timing.”

what_to_say: “Now we take that calm decision making into a movement game. This is not about winning. It is about staying composed.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
no punches
touch shoulder only
small movements
calm under changing speed

what_to_say: “You are trying to lightly touch the shoulder while defending from being touched. Stay in stance. No wild lunging. No turning away.”
what_to_explain:
Allowed defense:
step back
slip
pivot
Not allowed:
rough contact
lunging wildly
turning the back
running out of stance
what_to_watch:
who is too aggressive
who does not understand game
what_to_fix: Demonstrate one calm rep if needed.

what_to_say: “Go. Light shoulder touches only.”
what_to_watch:
stance
balance
overreaching
tension
eyes on partner
wild speed
what_to_fix:
If lunging:“Small moves.”
If standing still:“Keep moving.”
If turning away:“Eyes on partner.”
If too aggressive:“Light touches only.”
What to explain during round
“Calm athletes move better.”“Do not chase. Make them miss.”

what_to_say: “Now I control speed. When I say go, speed increases. When I say slow, you must reduce speed immediately.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
speed changes test composure
athletes must stay balanced even when tempo rises
what_to_watch: who looks nervous about speed change
what_to_fix: Remind:“Fast does not mean wild.”

what_to_say: “Go.”Then later:“Slow.”Then:“Go.”
what_to_watch:
panic on “go”
inability to slow down
balance loss
breathing getting erratic
what_to_fix:
If chaos on “go”:“Speed up without losing control.”
If they cannot slow:“Slow means controlled now.”
If balance lost:“Shorter steps.”
What to explain while coaching
“Control is the skill.”“Anyone can go wild. Good athletes stay organized.”

what_to_say: “Fast feet, 10 seconds. Stay upright. Hands up.”
what_to_watch:
hands dropping
athletes quitting early
posture collapsing
what_to_fix: “Hands up.”“Stay tall but athletic.”

what_to_say: “Back to glove tag. Keep the same control.”
what_to_watch:
fatigue changing behavior
frustration
sloppier stance
what_to_fix: If frustration rises:“Relax and reset.”

what_to_say: “Now we put the pattern on the bag. Defense first. Then offense. Then exit.”
what_to_explain:
Every rep has 3 parts:
defense
two punch combo
angle exit

what_to_say: “If you punch without defending first, it does not count.”
what_to_explain:
Options:
slip
roll
step back
Then:
two punches
Then:
small step left or right
what_to_watch:
bag spacing
athletes understanding sequence
what_to_fix: Demonstrate one rep if needed:“Slip, cross hook, step out.”

what_to_say: “Round 1. One pattern only. Slip, cross hook, step out.”
what_to_watch:
skipping defense
rushing punches
no exit
squaring up
heavy sloppy shots
what_to_fix:
If no defense:“Defense first.”
If no exit:“Finish and move.”
If sloppy punches:“Clean shots.”
If squared up:“Reset stance.”
What to explain during round
“Do not stay in front after you punch.”“Move with purpose, not panic.”

what_to_say: “Now you may use slip, roll, or step back, but every rep still needs defense, two punches, and an exit.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
freedom increases thinking
structure stays the same
do not add extra punches unless told
what_to_watch:
who handles variation well
who gets sloppy with freedom
what_to_fix: Keep fixed pattern for struggling athletes.

what_to_say: “Go. Defense, two punches, angle out.”
what_to_watch:
decision making
clean sequence
balance after exit
athletes punching too hard
what_to_fix:
If hard punching takes over:“Technique over power.”
If exit too large:“Small angle.”
If sequence breaks:“Defense, punch, move.”

what_to_say: “If you are looking good, coach may call left or right for your exit.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
this forces listening under movement
still keep everything controlled
what_to_watch:
listening skill
footwork quality on called exit
what_to_fix: If listening poor:“Wait for the call.”

what_to_say: “Last bag round. Stay clean. No rushing.”
what_to_watch:
fatigue effects
sloppy exits
athletes abandoning defense first rule
what_to_fix: “Defense first.”“Stay balanced.”“Reset after every rep.”

what_to_say:
“Bring it in.”
Ask:“What did you see before you moved today?”“Where did you feel rushed?”“What helped you stay calm?”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
being aware of what they felt helps learning
calm, correct reps matter more than flashy reps
what_to_watch:
are athletes giving thoughtful answers
who still seems amped up going into contact
what_to_fix:
If energy is too wild:“Contact block stays controlled. Same mindset.”
5:00 PM TO 6:00 PM
CONTACT SESSION

what_to_say: “This is controlled. We are applying what we just learned. Light work. Smart work. I will stop anything that gets too hard or too wild.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
goal is reading and execution
not ego
not power
not winning the round
what_to_watch:
emotional athletes
athletes too excited for sparring
what_to_fix: If intensity mindset is wrong:“We are learning, not fighting.”

what_to_say: “One partner gives cues. One reacts correctly. We are still seeing before moving.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
partner may call real or fake cues
responder must not bite on false information

what_to_say: “Go. Call and react.”
what_to_watch:
reacting to fake calls
poor stance
guessing
rushing
what_to_fix:
If reacting to fake:“Do not move unless you actually see it.”
If too robotic:“Stay relaxed.”

what_to_say: “This is technical sparring. Light contact. Controlled tempo. Reading first.”
what_to_explain:
Round 1:
jab only
Round 2:
jab and cross
Round 3:
open but controlled
what_to_watch: do athletes understand limits
what_to_fix: Ask one athlete:“What is the rule for Round 1?”

what_to_say: “Jab only. Read before you respond. Go.”
what_to_watch:
forcing action
chasing
poor defense
intensity too high
what_to_fix:
If chasing:“Let the opening come.”
If too hard:“Slow it down.”
If no defense:“Do not just trade jabs. Read and answer.”

what_to_say: “Round 2. Add the cross. Still light. Still controlled.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
cross should not make them reckless
defense still matters before counters

what_to_watch:
cross making them overcommit
loss of balance
escalation of power
panic counters
what_to_fix:
If overcommitting:“Stay under your hips.”
If hard counters:“Touch, do not blast.”
If balance poor:“Smaller shots, cleaner feet.”

what_to_say: “Round 3. Open, but same control. Reading first.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
freedom does not remove discipline
still light
still smart

what_to_watch:
who keeps structure
who loses patience
emotional decisions
hard shots sneaking in
what_to_fix:
If ego rises:“Settle down.”
If structure lost:“Go back to jab first.”

what_to_say: “Now we add rules. The rule matters more than winning.”
what_to_explain:
Round 1:
only score after a defensive action
Round 2:
start near ropes, escape first
Round 3:
last 30 seconds higher pace

what_to_say: “Defense before score. Go.”
what_to_watch:
forgetting rule
scoring without defense
rushing defense
fake defensive movement just to qualify
what_to_fix:
If they forget rule:“Does not count. Defense first.”
If defense fake:“Make it real. Actually evade or block.”

what_to_say: “Round 2. Start near ropes. Escape first, then attack.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
first task is position
offense starts after clean escape
do not swing from bad position

what_to_watch:
athletes attacking before escaping
poor footwork off ropes
panic when trapped
turning sideways badly
what_to_fix:
If attacking too early:“Get out first.”
If panic on ropes:“Small steps. Stay calm.”
If footwork poor:“Angle out, do not square up.”

what_to_say: “Round 3. Normal sparring, but last 30 seconds pick up tempo without losing form.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
faster does not mean sloppy
composure is still the test

what_to_watch:
control during pace increase
breathing
emotional reactions
form breakdown
what_to_fix:
If chaos appears:“Fast and clean, not fast and wild.”
If breathing poor:“Breathe and reset.”

what_to_say: “Now open spar. Seventy percent. I can stop this at any time.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
this is still a learning round
stay smooth
no hard hunting
control your emotions

what_to_watch:
power creep
frustration
loss of defense
loss of structure
what_to_fix:
If power too high:“Bring it down now.”
If frustration visible:“Relax. Breathe.”
If defense disappears:“See first, then work.”

what_to_say: “Ten second burst. Bag or shadow. Go.”
what_to_watch:
posture under fatigue
sloppy punching
quitting mentally
what_to_fix: “Stay clean even when tired.”

what_to_watch:
fatigue decisions
athletes rushing more
emotional exchanges
what_to_fix:
If rushed:“Slow your eyes down.”
If brawling starts:“Reset. Too messy.”

what_to_say: “Ten seconds. Fast but clean.”
what_to_watch: ability to follow command under fatigue
what_to_fix: If they go sloppy:“Clean first.”

what_to_watch:
who stays composed late
who falls apart under fatigue
who keeps reading instead of guessing
what_to_fix: Praise good examples:“Good patience.”“Good control.”“Good defense first.”

what_to_say: “Last block. Technique while tired.”
what_to_explain:
Round 1:
jab only, high volume
Round 2:
defend then two punches
Round 3:
free, but defense before offense
Last 20 seconds:
high output

what_to_watch:
jab quality
volume without collapse
hands dropping
posture
what_to_fix:
If jab gets sloppy:“Straight punches.”“Stay balanced.”
If hands drop:“Hands home after every jab.”

what_to_say: “Round 2. Defense before two punches.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
rule matters even when tired
tired is when discipline shows up

what_to_watch:
skipping defense
throwing wide shots
no reset
panic speed
what_to_fix:
If defense skipped:“Does not count. Defense first.”
If wide sloppy punches:“Shorter, cleaner punches.”

what_to_say: “Round 3. Free, but still defend first. Last 20 seconds are high output.”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
freedom does not remove structure
stay composed into fatigue

what_to_watch:
mental discipline
technical breakdown
emotional effort versus smart effort
what_to_fix:
If they get wild:“Stay smart while tired.”
If technique falls apart:“Lower speed, keep form.”

what_to_say:
“Bring it in.”
Ask:“What did you see better today?”“When did you feel rushed?”“What helped you stay composed?”
what_to_explain:
Explain:
good athletes reflect
today was about vision, calm, and control
better fighters are built by reading and responding, not by guessing
what_to_watch:
athlete understanding
emotional tone of room
whether lesson landed
what_to_fix:
If answers are weak:Summarize for them:“Today you worked on seeing first, controlling your reaction, and keeping technique while pressure increased.”
